Report_ID: Mental-health domain health-related quality of life (SF-12 MCS) at 6 months
Title: Life Goals Collaborative Care for Patients With Bipolar Disorder and Cardiovascular Disease Risk
Author: Kilbourne AM, Goodrich DE, Lai Z, Clogston J, Waxmonsky J, Bauer MS
Comment: Means/SDs are the 6-month descriptive endpoint values from Table 2 (LGCC listed first; group_1_is_control=False). The reported beta (.03, 95% CI -1.9 to 1.9), t=.03, df=51, p=.98 and d=.01 come from the overall repeated-measures model adjusting for baseline, treatment, time (6 and 12 months) and time x treatment, not from a 6-month-only contrast; therefore M_diff was left empty. Per-group Ns are the analysed Ns from Table 1 (randomised Ns were 34 per arm). Authors describe analyses as exploratory (pilot study).; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Life Goals Collaborative Care (LGCC)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
domain: psychiatry / collaborative care for severe mental illness
Participant type: Adults (age >=18) with bipolar disorder (type I, II or NOS) and >=1 cardiometabolic risk factor
Recruitment source: Two community-based mental health outpatient programs in southeastern Michigan (recruited 2009)
Outcome measurement: Endpoint (post-intervention) mean and SD per group at the 6-month follow-up, from Table 2
Outcome variable: Mental-health domain health-related quality of life (SF-12 MCS) at 6 months

Report_ID: SF-12 Mental Component Summary (MCS) at 6 months
Title: Collaborative care for schizophrenic patients in primary care: A double blind, randomized clinical trial of efficacy and safety
Author: Salman et al.
Comment: Per-group analysed Ns are not reported for Table 3; used the 46 vs 46 analysed sample stated in the Results ("46 in intervention group with 46 controlled group subjects"). Note Table 1 inconsistently lists n=39 usual care and n=41 collaborative care, and the randomised sizes were 46 vs 50. M_diff computed as group_2_mean − group_1_mean from explicitly reported two-group endpoint means. The follow-up MCS value of 68.31 is implausibly high for a norm-based SF-12 MCS; data quality uncertain. Text elsewhere mentions 3-month/week-12 assessments, but Table 3 is explicitly labelled "At 6 months".
Study Environment: clinical (hospital psychiatry ward with outpatient follow-up)
Participant type: Adults with schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder attending a hospital psychiatry ward/clinic
Recruitment source: Psychiatry ward, Lady Reading Hospital, Post Graduate Medical Institute, Peshawar, Pakistan
Outcome measurement: Mean (SD) MCS score per group at 6-month follow-up
Outcome variable: SF-12 Mental Component Summary (MCS) at 6 months

Report_ID: Mental-health domain health-related quality of life (WHOQOL-BREF psychological health domain score) at third follow-up
Title: Impact of Pharmacist–Psychiatrist Collaborative Patient Education on Medication Adherence and Quality of Life (QOL) of Bipolar Affective Disorder (BPAD) Patients
Author: Mishra et al.
Comment: M_diff computed as test minus control from the two explicitly reported endpoint means (simple two-group between-subjects design). Follow-ups were at ~1-month intervals, so the third follow-up is ~3 months — the nearest available to, and not later than, 6 months. Table 3 is formatted with shifted row labels; domain values recovered from the stated column order. Analysed Ns taken from Results text (38 test, 35 control). No standardized effect size reported by the paper.
Participant type: adult (≥18 years) outpatients diagnosed with bipolar affective disorder, without co-morbidities, literate
Recruitment source: Psychiatry outpatient department, tertiary care hospital (JSS Hospital), Mysore, South India
Outcome measurement: Endpoint (post-intervention) mean ± SD per group at third follow-up
Outcome variable: Mental-health domain health-related quality of life (WHOQOL-BREF psychological health domain score) at third follow-up
